local.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one independent research-guided hypothetical local illustration for Dimorphos, the small satellite of asteroid Didymos. Wide landscape composition about 1672 by 941. Low camera overlooking a compact uneven field of independently invented subdued grey angular boulders, coarse grains, shallow gaps and low irregular relief, black sky above, restrained oblique light and readable shadows. This is a generic invented local patch, not DART's impact site, not a reconstruction of any DRACO photograph, not measured post-impact geography. Do not use any reference image or copy/recolour any asteroid, Moon, Mars, Pluto or other body's map. Material fractions, mineral chemistry, grain/block sizes, grey colour, illumination, exposure, camera position and surface normal are invented. Do not depict ejecta plume, impact crater identification, a surviving spacecraft, people, equipment, liquid, ocean, biology, foreground atmosphere or survivable landing. No Didymos, Sun, stars, rings or other astronomical disk in this local view; absence from frame is artistic and is not physical absence. Do not imply a measured spin state, synchronous rotation or permanently Didymos-facing site; post-DART orbital changes do not establish those. Use a large legible bottom annotation band containing exactly two lines: 'IMAGINED — LOCAL VIEW FROM DIMORPHOS' and 'Terrain, materials, colour and lighting are hypothetical.' No other text.

sky.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Generate one completely independent hypothetical SKY FROM DIMORPHOS illustration, wide landscape about 1672 by 941 pixels. A low invented field of subdued grey angular boulders and coarse grains occupies only the bottom quarter, with black sky above. In the upper-middle sky show the distinct primary asteroid Didymos as a large complete roughly rounded but mildly irregular grey body, about 650 pixels across in this composition, fully separated from foreground and image borders. Schematic angular planning uses skyGeometry: primary radius .39 km, nominal separation 1.152 km minus assumed Dimorphos spherical camera height .0755 km gives centre distance 1.0765 km, angular diameter 42.4812069 degrees, nominal horizontal FOV90 degrees at width1672 gives target649.8896pixels. This is only hypothetical catalogue-scale planning, not a dated ephemeris, verified local normal, confidence interval or reconstructed measured silhouette. Didymos surface pattern, irregular silhouette, attitude, phase, grey colour and shadow are independently invented: restrained irregular relief and subtle texture, never reuse any Moon, Mars, Pluto, asteroid or other body's map. Keep the full primary outline discernible with oblique light; exposure and dark-side visibility artistic. Foreground Dimorphos geology, grain/block sizes, chemistry, material fractions, camera site and light are invented, not DART impact-site reconstruction or measured post-impact shape. Post-DART orbital period does not establish spin locking, permanent primary-facing ground or visibility from every site. No secondary moon, Sun, stars, rings, foreground atmosphere, clouds, plume, exposed liquid/ocean, biology, people, spacecraft or equipment; omissions are artistic framing not measured physical absence. No suggestion of survivable landing. A legible bottom annotation band must contain exactly two lines: 'IMAGINED — SKY FROM DIMORPHOS' and 'Terrain, Didymos appearance and lighting are hypothetical.' No other text.
